court: In the High Court of Madras
appellants: Hazrath Syed Basha Kathiri Kalandar Waliyullah Baba Dargah Represented by the Secretary, Syed Babu (M/55) … Petitioner(s);
respondents: Inspector of Police Vazhavanthinadu Police Station, Namakkal District and Another … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. S. Yogaraja Sekar
prayer: Prayer: Writ Petition (Criminal) filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to grant necessary permission and police protection for conducting the two day Santhanakoodu Urs Festival on 28-5-2026 and 29-5-2026 in the government land adjacent to the Dargah Premises, situated at Karavali, Kollimalai Taluk, Sndhamangalam, Namakkal District.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Mohammed Shaffiq, J.:— The present Writ Petition has been filed seeking a writ of mandamus to direct the respondents to grant necessary permission and adequate police protection for conducting the customary two-day annual Santhanakoodu Urs Festival at the “Hazrath Syed Basha Kathiri Kalandar Waliyullah Baba Dargah” situated at Kollimalai Adivaram Kaavalvali Area, Sendhamangalam Taluk, Namakkal District.

2. The petitioner initially scheduled the festival for 28-5-2026 and 29-5-2026, asserting a long-standing custom of utilizing the adjacent government land for public gatherings and religious ceremonies. The petitioner alleged that arbitrary single-day restrictions by the police authorities in recent years caused severe hardship, and further contended that the pendency of civil disputes regarding committee administration before the learned District Munsif Court, Sendhamangalam in O.S. No. 55 of 2025, should not be used as a ground to deny the fundamental religious rights of the devotees to participate in the annual festival.

3. During the pendency of this petition, it emerged that rival claims existed between factions led by Mr Shamsudeen Hussain and Mr M. Abdul Rahim regarding the administration and conduct of the festival, which had previously resulted in the festival not being conducted in the year 2025 despite Peace Committee talks before the Revenue Divisional Officer, Namakkal.

4. To ensure the peaceful conduct of the religious event, a joint compromise memo was entered into and signed by the rival parties, including Mr Shamsudeen Hussain and Mr M. Abdul Rahim, setting out an interim arrangement without prejudice to their respective rights and contentions in the pending civil suit. In paragraph No. 8 of the compromise memo, the revised dates and initial schedule for the festival were proposed as follows: 30-5-2026 (Saturday): 03.00 p.m. to 07.00 p.m. - Mawlid, Special Prayers, and Flag Hoisting Ceremonies. 31-5-2026 (Sunday): 10.00 p.m. to 05.00 a.m. - Religious gatherings, devotional programmes, distribution of food (Niyaz), and final Santhanakoodu Urs events.

5. The The learned government advocate raised serious objections to the proposed joint compromise memo, particularly emphasizing that the Dargah is situated within a Reserved Forest area. The State submitted that the petitioner's gathering or function should be conducted strictly in compliance with law. In particular, the The learned government advocate submitted that the proposal to hold religious gatherings and public participation between 10.00 p.m. and 5.00 a.m. is impermissible, as activities during night would cause distress, disturb, and severely unsettle the wildlife in the area.

6. This Court directs the following conditions which must be strictly adhered to by all parties:

(a) No public gatherings, religious assemblies, or public participation programmes shall take place between 10.00 p.m. and 5.00 a.m., and all daily outdoor ceremonies must conclude by 10:00 PM.

(b) The entire function shall be conducted without using any firecrackers or explosives, and the organizers shall ensure that noise levels remain strictly within permissible limits.

(c) No lights will be permitted in the open forest area, and illumination is strictly restricted to the inside of the Dargah premises.

(d) There shall be no dumping of garbage or food waste, and the organizers shall hold joint responsibility to ensure the forest area is fully preserved and cleaned up immediately after the daily programmes finish.

7. In light of the joint compromise memo and the subsequent undertakings made by all parties before this court, this Criminal Writ Petition is disposed of by directing the respondents to provide adequate police protection and necessary permission for the Santhanakoodu Urs Festival on 30-5-2026 and 31-5-2026, strictly in accordance with the modified timings and conditions set out above.

8. It is needless to mention that if the organizers or participants violate any of the conditions imposed by this Court including the nighttime ban, prohibition of firecrackers, noise levels, overlighting, or garbage disposal, the respondent police and forest authorities are at liberty to take immediate and appropriate legal action against them in accordance with law.

9. Mr Shamsudeen Hussain is at liberty to work out his remedies in the manner know to law for conducting similar functions in future.

10. Accordingly this Criminal Writ Petition stands disposed of in terms of the joint compromise memo as modified by this order. No costs.
